references.text: God promises Abraham that Ishmael will be fruitful and numerous, and that He will make him into a great nation—the same promise the angel repeats to Hagar.
The Lord's angel predicts that Hagar's descendants through Ishmael will become so numerous they cannot be counted, and describes Ishmael's character and future.
God assures Abraham that Ishmael will become a people because he is Abraham's son, which prepares for the promise repeated directly to Hagar.
Ishmael's genealogy shows the fulfillment of God's promise that he would become a great nation with twelve princes.
God was with the boy Ishmael, and he grew up and became an archer in the wilderness—an initial fulfillment of the promise concerning his future.
God's promise to make Isaac into a great nation is grounded in His eternal ability to uphold His chosen one with His own hand.
God's promise to lift up Isaac illustrates the general principle in Psalm 91 that He lifts up those who hold fast to Him.
Both verses demonstrate God's sovereign ability to create a 'great nation' from a single person or a situation of mortal threat.
The promise to make Isaac into a great nation is a direct confirmation and fulfillment of the original promise given to Abraham.
The promise to make Isaac into a great nation is a direct restatement and confirmation of the covenant promise given to Abraham in 17:6.
Both verses demonstrate God's sovereign ability to create a 'great nation' from a single person or a situation of mortal threat.
The promise to make Isaac into a great nation is a direct restatement and confirmation of the covenant promise given to Sarah in 17:16.
